dedupe_keys.name: ember europe electricity interconnection data cross border capacities import potentials and flows for 51 countries 2024 2030 2040

description: Ember, an energy think tank, publishes the data behind its Europe Electricity Interconnection Data Tool on the use (flows) and potential (capacity) of the cross-border transmission grid across Europe and neighbouring countries. The dataset covers 51 countries and holds interconnection capacities and import potentials by country for 2024, 2030 and 2040 in three cases: a best estimate, a high scenario in which all projects scheduled by 2030 or 2040 come online as planned, and viable needs, meaning the interconnection capacity that would minimise system costs for 2030 and 2040. It also gives flow patterns between countries and renewable generation and net export patterns by country, both for the best estimate only. The data are available as a free ZIP download from the dataset page, with a methodology PDF, an interactive data tool and a named analyst contact; Ember states that all its content is released under CC BY 4.0. Coverage is Europe and neighbouring countries. Caveats: future capacities depend on project schedules and Ember modelling, and the methodology PDF could not be text-extracted here, so sources and methods are described only as the page states. Simulation uses are cross-border capacity and flow inputs for European power system and adequacy models. Related records: data-entsos-tyndp-scenarios gives the official planning scenarios.
